model_scope: Early horizontal power loom, improvements of 1787–1790; educational reconstruction, not the vertical-warp prototype patented in 1785

images.prompt: Scientific educational museum illustration, landscape 3:2, a complete EARLY MECHANICAL POWER LOOM illustrating Edmund Cartwright's horizontal-warp improvements of 1787–1790, not the vertical-warp 1785 prototype and not a later Victorian Lancashire loom. Reference 1 is STYLE AND GENERAL WOODEN LOOM CONSTRUCTION ONLY: match warm oak, ivory backdrop, fine naturalistic materials, elegant soft daylight, front-left three-quarter oblique view. Reference 2 is a primary historical drawing of a portion of Cartwright's 1790 mechanism: use it for the principle of a lower rotating shaft, gears and tappets operating the shuttle springs and reed. The NEW object is an early wooden loom with a heavy four-post oak frame, rear warp beam and a horizontal sheet of cream warp, two heddle frames, front suspended beater and reed with a narrow shuttle race and small end boxes, boat-shaped shuttle carrying weft, and cloth wound on the front beam. Show a coherent iron lower cross-shaft running left-to-right in bearings, two visible lobed cam/tappet discs with followers connected upwards to the heddle levers, and a clearly visible side crank with a rod driving the beater. A single large wooden spoked drive wheel with a coaxial belt pulley stands on the right outside of the timber frame and connects to the lower drive shaft through a small visible gear pair. A narrow leather belt enters from above right and loops around this pulley, indicating external power without depicting an engine. Mechanical impulse rods lead to the two shuttle picker boxes. All axes, bearings, belt planes and connecting rods must be spatially coherent. Keep the main weaving path easy to see and the lower coordinating shaft unobscured. NO foot pedals, NO operator hand cord, NO person, NO electric motor, NO Jacquard head or punched cards, NO large Victorian cast iron sides. One whole assembled machine on pale ivory, generous margins, no floor setting, no text, arrows, numbers, inset panels or labels. This is a plausible educational reconstruction of the mechanical principle, not a claimed exact surviving specimen.

Edit target: the attached assembled early wooden Cartwright-type mechanical loom. Create an educational exploded view of THIS SAME object, preserving every part's exact size, shape, orientation, warm oak and iron materials and the identical front-left oblique camera. Landscape 3:2 pale warm ivory, museum-quality naturalistic illustration, soft shadows, generous margins. Keep the four-post wooden frame assembled centrally as the anchor. Gently separate ONLY five functional subassemblies by short straight translations: (1) the rear two heddle frames slightly upwards, together, with their cords; (2) the complete front beater/reed, shuttle race and end boxes slightly forward, with the shuttle still on its race; (3) the front cloth take-up beam slightly downward and forward; (4) the complete lower iron cross-shaft WITH its two cam discs, follower levers and bearings slightly down, staying horizontal and aligned with its original supports; (5) the large right-side wooden drive wheel, pulley and small driving gear slightly right, keeping the plane of the wheel unchanged. Keep all the transmission rods close to their mating subassemblies, still recognizable. Never rotate, rescale, multiply, omit or redesign components. Preserve the original horizontal warp path and recognizable complete machine silhouette; this should look gently opened out rather than a pile of objects. No extra gears or wheels. No text, labels, numbers, arrows, dashed lines, people, inset panels or pedals. Maintain the same elegant photographic illustration quality and restrained colors.
